claim: Borrelia burgdorferi (Bb) is the causative agent of Lyme disease.
source: Borrelia burgdorferi (Bb), the causative agent of Lyme disease, adapts to vastly different environments as it cycles between tick vector and vertebrate host.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established scientific knowledge about Lyme disease etiology.

claim: Bb adapts to vastly different environments as it cycles between tick vector and vertebrate host.
source: Borrelia burgdorferi (Bb), the causative agent of Lyme disease, adapts to vastly different environments as it cycles between tick vector and vertebrate host.
evidence: This is a well-established characteristic of Bb's lifecycle supported by scientific literature.

claim: During a tick bloodmeal, Bb alters its gene expression to prepare for vertebrate infection.
source: During a tick bloodmeal, Bb alters its gene expression to prepare for vertebrate infection; however, the full range of transcriptional changes that occur over several days inside of the tick are technically challenging to capture.
evidence: This is supported by prior research on Bb gene expression changes during transmission.

claim: The full range of transcriptional changes that occur over several days inside of the tick are technically challenging to capture.
source: During a tick bloodmeal, Bb alters its gene expression to prepare for vertebrate infection; however, the full range of transcriptional changes that occur over several days inside of the tick are technically challenging to capture.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical limitations of studying Bb in ticks, which is a known challenge in the field.

claim: The study developed an experimental approach to enrich Bb cells to longitudinally define their global transcriptomic landscape inside nymphal Ixodes scapularis ticks during a transmitting bloodmeal.
source: We developed an experimental approach to enrich Bb cells to longitudinally define their global transcriptomic landscape inside nymphal Ixodes scapularis ticks during a transmitting bloodmeal.
evidence: This describes the methodology developed in this study.

claim: 192 Bb genes substantially change expression over the course of the bloodmeal from 1 to 4 days after host attachment.
source: We identified 192 Bb genes that substantially change expression over the course of the bloodmeal from 1 to 4 days after host attachment.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNA-seq differential expression analysis presented in the study.

claim: The majority of upregulated genes encode proteins found at the cell envelope or proteins of unknown function.
source: The majority of upregulated genes encode proteins found at the cell envelope or proteins of unknown function, including 45 outer surface lipoproteins embedded in the unusual protein-rich coat of Bb.
evidence: This is based on functional categorization of the differentially expressed genes identified in the study.

claim: 45 outer surface lipoproteins are embedded in the unusual protein-rich coat of Bb and are among the upregulated genes.
source: The majority of upregulated genes encode proteins found at the cell envelope or proteins of unknown function, including 45 outer surface lipoproteins embedded in the unusual protein-rich coat of Bb.
evidence: This is derived from analysis of the upregulated genes and their functional annotations.

claim: Mass spectrometry was utilized to identify candidate tick proteins that physically associate with Bb.
source: As these proteins may facilitate Bb interactions with the host, we utilized mass spectrometry to identify candidate tick proteins that physically associate with Bb.
evidence: This describes the mass spectrometry experiments performed in the study.

claim: Lyme disease is the most reported vector-borne disease in North America.
source: Lyme disease, the most reported vector-borne disease in North America, is caused by the bacterial pathogen Borrelia burgdorferi (Bb) (Rosenberg et al., 2018; Steere et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to epidemiological studies.

claim: The primary vector of Bb is the blacklegged tick Ixodes scapularis.
source: Its primary vector, the blacklegged tick Ixodes scapularis, acquires and transmits Bb through two separate multi-day bloodmeals, one in which Bb is acquired from an infected vertebrate host and a second, during the subsequent life stage, in which Bb is transmitted to a new host (Tilly et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Bb transmission supported by citation.

claim: Ixodes scapularis acquires and transmits Bb through two separate multi-day bloodmeals.
source: Its primary vector, the blacklegged tick Ixodes scapularis, acquires and transmits Bb through two separate multi-day bloodmeals, one in which Bb is acquired from an infected vertebrate host and a second, during the subsequent life stage, in which Bb is transmitted to a new host (Tilly et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the lifecycle of Bb transmission through ticks, supported by citation.

claim: During the transmission bloodmeal, Bb proliferates in the tick midgut before a subset of these cells disseminate to the salivary glands.
source: During the transmission bloodmeal, Bb proliferates in the tick midgut before a subset of these cells disseminate to the salivary glands (Dunham-Ems et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on Bb migration in ticks.

claim: Bb is deposited into the new host via the tick saliva extruded into the bite site.
source: Bb is deposited into the new host via the tick saliva extruded into the bite site (Ribeiro et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citation describing the mechanism of Bb transmission.

claim: When an infected tick feeds, Bb responds to bloodmeal-induced environmental changes and undergoes cellular modifications driven by key transcriptional circuits, including the RpoN/RpoS sigma factor cascade and the Hk1/Rrp1 two-component system.
source: When an infected tick feeds, Bb responds to bloodmeal-induced environmental changes and undergoes cellular modifications driven by key transcriptional circuits, including the RpoN/RpoS sigma factor cascade and the Hk1/Rrp1 two-component system (Radolf et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on Bb transcriptional regulation.

claim: In vitro analyses of Bb cells cultured in tick- or mammal-like growth conditions have revealed widespread transcriptome remodeling during host switching.
source: In vitro analyses of Bb cells cultured in tick- or mammal-like growth conditions have pointed to additional genetic determinants of tick-borne transmission by revealing widespread transcriptome remodeling during host switching (reviewed in Samuels et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review summarizing prior in vitro studies.

claim: It is not fully clear how in vitro expression changes correspond to complex in vivo changes over the course of a transmission bloodmeal.
source: However, it is not fully clear how these in vitro expression changes correspond to complex in vivo changes over the course of a transmission bloodmeal.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that motivates the current study.

claim: Capturing comprehensive, longitudinal data on Bb gene expression from inside its vector has been hampered by technical challenges due to the dynamic nature of the bloodmeal and the general low abundance of bacterial cells relative to the tick.
source: Capturing comprehensive, longitudinal data on Bb gene expression from inside its vector has been hampered by technical challenges due to the dynamic nature of the bloodmeal and the general low abundance of bacterial cells relative to the tick (Samuels et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes technical challenges in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Bb sequence enrichment coupled with microarrays identified large scale changes in Bb gene expression between the first and second tick bloodmeals.
source: Bb sequence enrichment coupled with microarrays identified large scale changes in Bb gene expression between the first and second tick bloodmeals (Iyer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a prior study using microarrays.

claim: Enriching Bb sequences from infected tick RNA-seq libraries through TBDCapSeq has provided clearer resolution into differences in Bb gene expression as it cycles between the fed tick and mammalian host.
source: More recently, enriching Bb sequences from infected tick RNA-seq libraries through TBDCapSeq has provided clearer resolution into differences in Bb gene expression as it cycles between the fed tick and mammalian host (Grassmann et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent study using TBDCapSeq.

claim: We have limited temporal resolution into the molecular transitions that happen across key steps of tick feeding.
source: Still, we have limited temporal resolution into the molecular transitions that happen across key steps of tick feeding.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Several specific tick–Bb protein–protein interactions are important for Bb survival, migration, or transmission to the next host.
source: Notably, several specific tick–Bb protein–protein interactions are important for Bb survival, migration, or transmission to the next host.
evidence: This is supported by prior research on tick-Bb interactions.

claim: OspA binds a tick cell surface protein, tick receptor for OspA (TROSPA), which is required for successful Bb colonization of the tick midgut during the first acquisition bloodmeal.
source: One of these proteins, OspA, binds a tick cell surface protein, tick receptor for OspA (TROSPA), which is required for successful Bb colonization of the tick midgut during the first acquisition bloodmeal (Pal et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to research on OspA-TROSPA interaction.

claim: BBE31 binds a tick protein TRE31, and disruption of this interaction decreases the number of Bb cells that successfully migrate from the tick gut to salivary glands.
source: For example, BBE31 binds a tick protein TRE31, and disruption of this interaction decreases the number of Bb cells that successfully migrate from the tick gut to salivary glands (Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to research on BBE31-TRE31 interaction.

claim: These interactions alone are not sufficient to block Bb growth or migration in ticks, suggesting there are likely additional molecular factors from Bb and ticks at play during tick-borne transmission.
source: However, these interactions alone are not sufficient to block Bb growth or migration in ticks, suggesting there are likely additional molecular factors from Bb and ticks at play during tick-borne transmission.
evidence: This is an inference based on the incomplete blocking of Bb transmission by known interactions.

claim: Initial attempts to uncover Bb mRNA by simply removing tick mRNA with polyA-depletion and removing tick rRNA sequences using DASH resulted in an average of only 0.09% of RNA-seq reads mapping to Bb mRNA.
source: Our initial attempts to uncover Bb mRNA by simply removing tick mRNA with polyA-depletion and removing tick rRNA sequences using Depletion of Abundant Sequences by Hybridization (DASH; Dynerman et al., 2020; Gu et al., 2016) were unsuccessful. This approach resulted in an average of only 0.09% of RNA-seq reads mapping to Bb mRNA – approximately 10-fold less than we estimated would be needed to feasibly obtain robust transcriptome-wide differential gene expression analysis (Haas et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the results of initial experimental attempts in the study.

claim: The αBb antibody specifically recognized several Bb proteins, including surface protein OspA.
source: By western blot analysis, we confirmed that αBb specifically recognized several Bb proteins, including surface protein OspA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which is highly prevalent on the Bb surface in the tick (Ohnishi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and citation.

claim: OspA is highly prevalent on the Bb surface in the tick.
source: By western blot analysis, we confirmed that αBb specifically recognized several Bb proteins, including surface protein OspA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which is highly prevalent on the Bb surface in the tick (Ohnishi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Immunofluorescence microscopy with αBb showed clear recognition of Bb cells from within the tick at each day of feeding.
source: In addition, immunofluorescence microscopy with αBb showed clear recognition of Bb cells from within the tick at each day of feeding (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Over 95% of total Bb flaB RNA was present in enriched fractions after immunomagnetic enrichment.
source: Measuring Bb flaB RNA from both Bb-enriched samples and their matched Bb-depleted fractions, we found over 95% of total Bb flaB RNA was present in enriched fractions (Figure 1C), suggesting our approach captured the vast majority of Bb transcripts from the tick.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: DASH reduced unwanted sequences from 94% to 9% of total libraries.
source: DASH reduced unwanted sequences from 94% to 9% of our total libraries, greatly increasing the relative abundance of Bb transcripts (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Between 0.6% and 3.4% of reads mapped to annotated Bb genic regions in the resulting libraries.
source: For resulting libraries generated across feeding, between 0.6% and 3.4% of reads mapped to annotated Bb genic regions (Figure 1E), which translated to an average of 4.3 million Bb genic reads per sample (Figure 1F and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: An average of 4.3 million Bb genic reads per sample were obtained.
source: For resulting libraries generated across feeding, between 0.6% and 3.4% of reads mapped to annotated Bb genic regions (Figure 1E), which translated to an average of 4.3 million Bb genic reads per sample (Figure 1F and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: At least 10 reads mapped to 92% of annotated Bb protein coding genes and pseudogenes across all samples from the 4 days.
source: Across all samples from the 4 days, at least 10 reads mapped to 92% of annotated Bb protein coding genes and pseudogenes.
evidence: This describes the coverage achieved in the RNA-seq experiment.

claim: Minimal expression differences were found when comparing RNA-seq libraries from in vitro cultured Bb cells before and after immunomagnetic enrichment (29 genes with p<0.05, fold changes between 0.83 and 1.12).
source: To evaluate whether our approach introduced any major artifacts in Bb expression, we sequenced and compared RNA-seq libraries from in vitro cultured Bb cells before and after immunomagnetic enrichment. We found minimal expression differences (29 genes with p<0.05, fold changes between 0.83 and 1.12; Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2—source data 1), suggesting experimental enrichment did not significantly alter global transcriptome profiles for Bb.
evidence: This is supported by differential expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Experimental enrichment did not significantly alter global transcriptome profiles for Bb.
source: We found minimal expression differences (29 genes with p<0.05, fold changes between 0.83 and 1.12; Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2—source data 1), suggesting experimental enrichment did not significantly alter global transcriptome profiles for Bb.
evidence: This is an inference based on the minimal expression differences observed in the control experiment.

claim: The first principal component, which explained 64% of the variance in the data, correlated well with day of feeding.
source: The first principal component, which explained 64% of the variance in our data, correlated well with day of feeding (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Bb gene expression changes generally trended in the same direction over the course of feeding with the most dramatic differences between flanking timepoints on day 1 and day 4.
source: The global pattern suggested that Bb gene expression changes generally trended in the same direction over the course of feeding with the most dramatic differences between flanking timepoints on day 1 and day 4.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the PCA results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: By day 4, there were 186 DE genes, including 153 upregulated and 33 downregulated compared to day 1.
source: By day 4, there were 186 DE genes, including 153 upregulated and 33 downregulated (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is supported by differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Across all later time point comparisons to day 1, 192 DE genes in total were found.
source: In the day 2, day 3, and day 4 comparisons to the day 1 baseline, we found 192 DE genes in total (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is the total number of differentially expressed genes identified across all comparisons.

claim: The expression of rpoS increased between day 1 and day 4.
source: Between day 1 and day 4, the expression of rpoS increased (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), as expected (Hübner et al., 2001), and the majority of genes activated by RpoS in the feeding tick (Grassmann et al., 2023), including canonical targets ospC and dbpA, were also significantly upregulated (79/89, p<0.05, Wald tests; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and citation.

claim: The majority of genes activated by RpoS in the feeding tick, including canonical targets ospC and dbpA, were significantly upregulated (79/89, p<0.05).
source: Between day 1 and day 4, the expression of rpoS increased (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), as expected (Hübner et al., 2001), and the majority of genes activated by RpoS in the feeding tick (Grassmann et al., 2023), including canonical targets ospC and dbpA, were also significantly upregulated (79/89, p<0.05, Wald tests; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by differential expression analysis and comparison to prior studies shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The majority of genes activated or repressed by Rrp1 in vitro also trended in the expected direction ex vivo between day 1 and day 4 (111/148 upregulated, 37/57 downregulated, p<0.05).
source: The majority of genes activated or repressed by Rrp1 in vitro (Caimano et al., 2015) also trended in the expected direction ex vivo between day 1 and day 4 (111/148 upregulated, 37/57 downregulated, p<0.05, Wald tests, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by differential expression analysis and comparison to prior studies shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 31% of the DE genes upregulated from day 1 (49/158) were more highly expressed in 'fed tick' conditions compared to 'unfed tick' conditions in one or both previous studies.
source: 31% of the DE genes upregulated from day 1 (49/158) were more highly expressed in 'fed tick' conditions compared to 'unfed tick' conditions in one or both studies, while 24% of the DE genes downregulated from day 1 (8/24) were more highly expressed in 'unfed tick' conditions in one or both studies (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to prior in vitro studies.

claim: 70% of DE genes upregulated on day 2 (21/30) were more highly expressed in 'fed tick' conditions in previous studies.
source: The studies become more concordant when focusing on the DE genes that were upregulated on day 2, which were generally the genes that changed the most dramatically in the time course. 70% of DE genes upregulated on day 2 (21/30) were more highly expressed in 'fed tick' conditions in these previous studies, suggesting that the majority of the most dramatic gene expression changes we saw across feeding agree with what was observed in these previous studies.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to prior in vitro studies.

claim: 63% of all upregulated DE genes (100/158) were differentially expressed between fed nymphs and DMCs in one or both previous studies.
source: We also compared the DE genes to two studies that assessed Bb gene expression differences in fed nymphs versus dialysis membrane chambers (DMCs), which mimic Bb conditions in the mammal (Grassmann et al., 2023; Iyer et al., 2015). 63% of all upregulated DE genes (100/158) were differentially expressed between fed nymphs and DMCs in one or both studies (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to prior studies comparing fed nymphs and DMCs.

claim: 14% of the twofold DE genes were not previously found to change expression in different tick-feeding contexts or identified as dependent upon RpoS, Rrp1, or RelBbu.
source: Through comparisons to these previous studies, we were able to verify that our data captured many expected transcriptional trends occurring during tick feeding. Nevertheless, 14% of the twofold DE genes were not previously found to change expression in these different tick-feeding contexts (Grassmann et al., 2023; Iyer et al., 2015; Ojaimi et al., 2003; Revel et al., 2002) or identified in these RNA-seq studies as dependent upon RpoS, Rrp1, or RelBbu (Caimano et al., 2015; Drecktrah et al., 2015; Grassmann et al., 2023), which are three known Bb regulatory programs active in the tick (Samuels et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to multiple prior studies.

claim: Most of the upregulated genes were located on the plasmids (143/158; 90%).
source: Consistent with these previous reports, we found that most of the upregulated genes were located on the plasmids (143/158; 90%), while fewer were found on the chromosome (15/158; 10%; Figure 3B), which is home to the majority of metabolic and other housekeeping genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the genomic locations of differentially expressed genes shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The majority of the downregulated genes were found on the chromosome (27/34, 79%).
source: In contrast, the majority of the downregulated genes were found on the chromosome (27/34, 79%; Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the genomic locations of differentially expressed genes shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Linear plasmid 54 (lp54) contained the largest number of upregulated genes.
source: Linear plasmid 54 (lp54), which is an essential plasmid present in all Bb isolates (Casjens et al., 2012), contained the largest number of upregulated genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the genomic locations of differentially expressed genes and citation.

claim: Many of the genes on lp54 are regulated by RpoS during feeding, including those encoding adhesins DbpA and DbpB, which are important for infectivity in the host.
source: Many of the genes on lp54 are regulated by RpoS during feeding, including those encoding adhesins DbpA and DbpB, which are important for infectivity in the host (Blevins et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on RpoS regulation and DbpA/DbpB function.

claim: BBA64 and BBA66 are necessary for optimal transmission via the tick bite.
source: This set also included five members of a paralogous family of outer surface lipoproteins BBA64, BBA65, BBA66, BBA71, and BBA73. BBA64 and BBA66 are necessary for optimal transmission via the tick bite (Gilmore et al., 2010; Patton et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on BBA64 and BBA66 function.

claim: Of the genes that increased twofold over feeding, the clear majority each day of feeding fell into two broad categories, cell envelope (55 of 158 total genes) and proteins of unknown function (69 of 158 total genes).
source: Of the genes that increased twofold over feeding, the clear majority each day of feeding fell into two broad categories, cell envelope (55 of 158 total genes) and proteins of unknown function (69 of 158 total genes), with fewer genes related to metabolism, chemotaxis and motility, transporters, bacteriophage, cell division, and transcription (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on functional categorization of differentially expressed genes shown in Figure 4A.

claim: More than half (46 of 83) of annotated outer surface lipoproteins changed expression twofold over the time course.
source: We found that more than half (46 of 83) of annotated outer surface lipoproteins (Dowdell et al., 2017; Iyer et al., 2015) changed expression twofold over the time course (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of outer surface lipoprotein expression shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 256 proteins (251 from I. scapularis and 5 from Bb) were enriched with Bb from infected ticks one day after attachment.
source: We found 256 proteins (251 from I. scapularis and 5 from Bb) that were enriched with Bb from infected ticks one day after attachment and 226 proteins (220 from I. scapularis and 6 from Bb) that were enriched with Bb from infected ticks four days after attachment (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of Bb-enriched samples.

claim: 226 proteins (220 from I. scapularis and 6 from Bb) were enriched with Bb from infected ticks four days after attachment.
source: We found 256 proteins (251 from I. scapularis and 5 from Bb) that were enriched with Bb from infected ticks one day after attachment and 226 proteins (220 from I. scapularis and 6 from Bb) that were enriched with Bb from infected ticks four days after attachment (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of Bb-enriched samples.

claim: Only 27 proteins (24 from I. scapularis and 3 from Bb) were detectable on both day 1 and day 4.
source: Of these proteins, only 27 (24 from I. scapularis and 3 from Bb) were detectable on both days, suggesting the tick proteins present upon Bb enrichment change dramatically over the course of feeding (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: OspC was identified in the samples from day 4 after attachment but not day 1 after attachment.
source: Amongst the small number of Bb proteins, we identified OspC in the samples from day 4 after attachment but not day 1 after attachment, confirming the expression change we saw in our RNA-seq.
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis and confirms RNA-seq results.

claim: Of the proteins found exclusively one day after attachment, 10 were categorized as extracellular matrix proteins, and this category was statistically enriched (Fisher's exact test, FDR = 0.000093).
source: Nevertheless, of the proteins found exclusively one day after attachment, 10 were categorized as extracellular matrix proteins using the PANTHER gene database (Thomas et al., 2022), and this category was statistically enriched (Fisher's exact test, FDR = 0.000093; Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This is based on functional enrichment analysis of mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Four days after attachment, 31 proteins were identified that are likely to be found at the membrane, including two proteins annotated as putative low-density lipoprotein receptors.
source: Four days after attachment, we did not detect any annotated extracellular matrix proteins; however, we identified 31 proteins that are likely to be found at the membrane, including two proteins annotated as putative low-density lipoprotein receptors (Figure 5C and Figure 5—source data 3).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Bb has a complex, highly fragmented genome including numerous plasmids that are necessary during specific stages of the enzootic cycle.
source: Bb has a complex, highly fragmented genome (Barbour, 1988; Figure 3A), including numerous plasmids that are necessary during specific stages of the enzootic cycle (Schwartz et al., 2021) suggesting they contain genes that are crucial for pathogen transmission and survival.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on Bb genome structure and plasmid function.

claim: Many genes found on the plasmids have been previously shown to alter expression upon environmental changes or in different host environments.
source: In fact, many genes found on the plasmids have been previously shown to alter expression upon environmental changes or in different host environments (Iyer et al., 2015; Ojaimi et al., 2005; Revel et al., 2002; Tokarz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: Bb strain B31-S9 harbors seven cp32 isoforms that are highly similar to each other.
source: Bb strain B31-S9 harbors seven cp32 isoforms that are highly similar to each other (Casjens et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on Bb genome structure.

claim: When cp32 prophages are induced, phage virions called ϕBB1 are produced.
source: When cp32 prophages are induced, phage virions called ϕBB1 are produced (Eggers and Samuels, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on cp32 prophages.

claim: Some cp32 genes have been shown to change expression in response to the presence of blood.
source: Some cp32 genes have been shown to change expression in response to the presence of blood (Tokarz et al., 2004) and as a part of the stringent response regulated by RelBbu (Drecktrah et al., 2015), while BBD18 and RpoS regulate prophage production in the tick midgut after feeding (Wachter et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on cp32 gene regulation.

claim: BBD18 and RpoS regulate prophage production in the tick midgut after feeding.
source: Some cp32 genes have been shown to change expression in response to the presence of blood (Tokarz et al., 2004) and as a part of the stringent response regulated by RelBbu (Drecktrah et al., 2015), while BBD18 and RpoS regulate prophage production in the tick midgut after feeding (Wachter et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Some prophage genes are upregulated over the course of tick feeding, raising the possibility that cp32 prophage are induced towards the end of feeding.
source: Our data suggest that some prophage genes are upregulated over the course of tick feeding, raising the possibility that cp32 prophage are induced towards the end of feeding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of upregulated prophage genes in the RNA-seq data.

claim: The Bb outer surface is covered with lipoproteins.
source: The Bb outer surface is covered with lipoproteins (Figure 4B), and these proteins are critical determinants in Bb interactions with the various environments encountered during the enzootic cycle (Kurokawa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research and is established knowledge about Bb cell structure.

claim: Outer surface lipoproteins are critical determinants in Bb interactions with the various environments encountered during the enzootic cycle.
source: The Bb outer surface is covered with lipoproteins (Figure 4B), and these proteins are critical determinants in Bb interactions with the various environments encountered during the enzootic cycle (Kurokawa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: ospA, ospB, ospC, and bba59 were the most highly expressed outer surface protein genes.
source: The magnitude of expression varied greatly, with ospA, ospB, ospC, and bba59 being the most highly expressed outer surface protein genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of expression levels shown in Figure 4C.

claim: During the bloodmeal, Bb are undergoing a complex outer surface transformation driven by increases in transcription of a majority of the genes encoding lipoproteins.
source: While bulk RNA-seq cannot distinguish what is happening at the single-cell level, our data suggest that during the bloodmeal, Bb are undergoing a complex outer surface transformation driven by increases in transcription of a majority of the genes encoding these lipoproteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that many outer surface lipoprotein genes are upregulated.

claim: Tick-Bb interactions are likely crucial at the beginning of the tick bloodmeal, as Bb adhere to the tick gut epithelium before becoming motile and migrating out of the midgut and into the salivary glands.
source: Tick-Bb interactions are likely crucial at the beginning of the tick bloodmeal, as Bb adhere to the tick gut epithelium before becoming motile and migrating out of the midgut and into the salivary glands (Dunham-Ems et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on Bb migration in ticks.

claim: Some Bb outer surface proteins, such as BBE31 and BBA52 play key roles in pathogen migration through interactions with the tick environment.
source: Some Bb outer surface proteins, such as BBE31 and BBA52 play key roles in pathogen migration through interactions with the tick environment (reviewed in Kurokawa et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review summarizing prior research.

claim: The vast majority of all detected proteins in the mass spectrometry analysis were from ticks (2801/2858, 98%).
source: When querying against the Bb and I. scapularis proteomes, we identified between 414 and 2240 protein groups per sample replicate. The vast majority of all detected proteins were from ticks (2801/2858, 98%).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis.

claim: The longitudinal collection of transcriptomes for Bb cells isolated from ticks serves as a resource and starting point for delineating the functional determinants of Bb adaptation and transmission.
source: Our longitudinal collection of transcriptomes for Bb cells isolated from ticks serves as a resource and starting point for delineating the functional determinants of Bb adaptation and transmission.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the dataset generated in this study.

claim: The transcriptome profiles revealed changes in expression of 26 genes not observed in previous studies.
source: While these genes were highly concordant with those found in previous studies probing transcriptional changes throughout the Bb enzootic cycle (Caimano et al., 2019; Caimano et al., 2015; Drecktrah et al., 2015; Grassmann et al., 2023; Iyer et al., 2015; Ojaimi et al., 2003; Revel et al., 2002), our transcriptome profiles revealed changes in expression of 26 genes not observed in these previous studies.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to multiple prior studies.

claim: Nine additional genes encoding cell envelope proteins were upregulated over feeding that were not found to change expression in previous studies examining conditions mimicking unfed ticks versus fed ticks or in nymphs versus DMCs.
source: Our data reveal more extensive expression changes for Bb outer surface proteins than previously appreciated, with nine additional genes encoding cell envelope proteins upregulated over feeding that were not found to change expression in the previous studies examining conditions mimicking unfed ticks versus fed ticks or in nymphs versus DMCs.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to prior studies.

claim: The extensive changes in genes encoding outer surface proteins suggest Bb is actively remodeling its outer coat to navigate the dynamic tick environment during feeding.
source: The extensive changes in genes encoding outer surface proteins suggest Bb is actively remodeling its outer coat to navigate the dynamic tick environment during feeding, akin to wardrobe changes across seasons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of extensive outer surface protein gene expression changes.

claim: Modifications to the Bb surface could facilitate different tick–pathogen interactions that are critical for its physical movement through tick compartments.
source: Modifications to the Bb surface could facilitate different tick–pathogen interactions that are critical for its physical movement through tick compartments.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional consequences of observed outer surface changes.

claim: Protective vaccines against vector-borne pathogens have often targeted surface proteins encoded by pathogens.
source: Protective vaccines against vector-borne pathogens have often targeted surface proteins encoded by pathogens (Kovacs-Simon et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on vaccine development.

claim: Previous Lyme disease vaccine efforts effectively targeted the highly expressed Bb outer surface protein OspA.
source: While previous Lyme disease vaccine efforts effectively targeted the highly expressed Bb outer surface protein OspA (Steere et al., 1998), more targets could increase the likelihood of a successful vaccine.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on Lyme disease vaccines.

claim: The study provides a catalog of new Bb candidates that could be explored for vaccine development.
source: Our study provides a catalog of new Bb candidates that could be explored.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential application of the study's findings.

claim: The biochemical pull-downs using tick-isolated Bb cells as bait unearthed a preliminary list of potential tick proteins that could be involved in tick–Bb interactions.
source: In addition, our biochemical pull-downs using tick-isolated Bb cells as bait unearthed a preliminary list of potential tick proteins that could be involved in tick–Bb interactions.
evidence: This describes the results of the mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: Blocking molecular interactions that are functionally critical for transmission could be explored as a therapeutic strategy.
source: Blocking molecular interactions that are functionally critical for transmission could also be explored as a therapeutic strategy (Barillas-Mury et al., 2022; Manning and Cantaert, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on therapeutic strategies and is speculation about potential applications.

claim: The αBb antibody captured the vast majority, but not all, Bb flaB transcripts from inside of the tick.
source: The αBb antibody, which targets OspA and a number of other proteins, captured the vast majority, but not all, Bb flaB transcripts from inside of the tick. This loss may introduce some degree of bias.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR results showing >95% capture and acknowledges potential limitations.

claim: A large number of day 4 reads mapping to P. fulva suggests that the αBb antibody may enrich other bacterial species.
source: Further, a large number of day 4 reads mapping to P. fulva suggests that this particular antibody may enrich other bacterial species.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of P. fulva reads in day 4 samples.

claim: The method was unable to produce consistent expression data from Bb from unfed ticks.
source: It is also important to note that our method was unable to produce consistent expression data from Bb from unfed ticks, limiting the full longitudinal scope of the study and potentially overlooking key changes occurring in the first 24 hours of feeding.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the methodology.

claim: The difficulty in obtaining data from unfed ticks may be due to low numbers of Bb in flat nymphs or the stress of the prolonged nutrient-deprived period between tick feedings.
source: We predict this difficulty may be due to low numbers of Bb in flat nymphs (de Silva and Fikrig, 1995) or the stress of the prolonged nutrient-deprived period between tick feedings (Kung et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation about the reasons for the technical difficulty, supported by citations.

claim: Strikingly few Bb cells out of the total pathogen population in ticks are ultimately transmitted to the next host during feeding.
source: Strikingly few Bb cells out of the total pathogen population in ticks are ultimately transmitted to the next host during feeding (Dunham-Ems et al., 2009; Rego et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on Bb transmission.

claim: There may be important molecular variations across Bb cells within the population residing in the tick that contribute to differential transmission outcomes.
source: There may be important molecular variations across Bb cells within the population residing in the tick that contribute to these differential outcomes including heterogeneously expressed proteins across cells within the feeding tick midgut (Ohnishi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is speculation about heterogeneity in the Bb population, supported by citation.

claim: Genes that appear unaltered or show low expression levels across the bulk population could still play an outsized role in infection for a minority of the cells.
source: Genes that appear unaltered or show low expression levels across the bulk population could still play an outsized role in infection for a minority of the cells, and conducting transcriptomic analyses at the single-cell level will be key.
evidence: This is speculation about the limitations of bulk RNA-seq and the potential importance of single-cell analysis.

claim: For samples pulled from the mice one, two, and three days after attachment, the majority of the remaining sequencing reads mapped to the I. scapularis genome (72–83%).
source: As expected, for samples pulled from the mice one, two, and three days after attachment, the majority of the remaining sequencing reads mapped to the I. scapularis genome (72–83%; Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on mapping sequencing reads to the tick genome.

claim: On day 4, when ticks were fully engorged and were recovered from mouse cages rather than pulled from the mice, fewer reads mapped to the I. scapularis genome (24–44%).
source: On day 4, when ticks were fully engorged and were recovered from mouse cages rather than pulled from the mice, we found that fewer reads mapped to the I. scapularis genome (24–44%).
evidence: This is based on mapping sequencing reads to the tick genome.

claim: Only a small percentage of reads from all samples mapped to the host Mus musculus genome (1–3%).
source: Only a small percentage of reads from all samples mapped to the host Mus musculus genome (1–3%).
evidence: This is based on mapping sequencing reads to the mouse genome.

claim: A large percentage of day 4 reads mapped to bacterial species Pseudomonas fulva (41–64%).
source: This analysis led us to discover that a large percentage of day 4 reads mapped to bacterial species Pseudomonas fulva (41–64%) (Figure 1—source data 1), which may have been present in our mouse cages.
evidence: This is based on analysis using CZ ID to identify the source of unmapped reads.

claim: The median number of reads per gene in each sample varied from 338 to 1167 reads.
source: The median number of reads per gene in each sample varied from 338 to 1167 reads (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This describes the sequencing depth achieved in the study.

claim: Of the DE genes that increased on day 2, 29 of 30 were still increased on day 3, and 29 of 30 were still increased on day 4.
source: For example, of the DE genes that increased on day 2, 29 of 30 were still increased on day 3, and 29 of 30 were still increased on day 4.
evidence: This describes the consistency of gene expression changes across timepoints.

claim: This is the first comprehensive report of global Bb expression changes over multiple stages of a tick feeding.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive report of global Bb expression changes over multiple stages of a tick feeding.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study's findings.

claim: About half of RelBbu-regulated genes changed in the direction expected if the stringent response was active during this time (129/251 upregulated, 111/226 downregulated, p<0.05).
source: We also examined the expression trends of genes regulated by RelBbu as part of the stringent response, another major transcriptional program active in Bb in the tick during nutrient starvation (Drecktrah et al., 2015). About half of RelBbu-regulated genes changed in the direction expected if the stringent response was active during this time (129/251 upregulated, 111/226 downregulated, p<0.05, Wald tests) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D); however, more of the genes that were twofold downregulated over feeding are regulated by RelBbu than either RpoS or Rrp1, suggesting it may play a role during this time frame.
evidence: This is based on comparison to prior studies on RelBbu regulation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: More of the genes that were twofold downregulated over feeding are regulated by RelBbu than either RpoS or Rrp1, suggesting it may play a role during this time frame.
source: About half of RelBbu-regulated genes changed in the direction expected if the stringent response was active during this time (129/251 upregulated, 111/226 downregulated, p<0.05, Wald tests) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D); however, more of the genes that were twofold downregulated over feeding are regulated by RelBbu than either RpoS or Rrp1, suggesting it may play a role during this time frame.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that downregulated genes are enriched for RelBbu targets.

claim: The genes that were more highly expressed in nymphs were most concentrated amongst the day 2 DE genes (17/30, 57%).
source: The genes that were more highly expressed in nymphs were most concentrated amongst the day 2 DE genes (17/30, 57%), while the genes more highly expressed in DMCs were concentrated amongst the day 3 and day 4 DE genes (55/128, 43%).
evidence: This is based on comparison to prior studies on gene expression in nymphs versus DMCs.

claim: The genes more highly expressed in DMCs were concentrated amongst the day 3 and day 4 DE genes (55/128, 43%).
source: The genes that were more highly expressed in nymphs were most concentrated amongst the day 2 DE genes (17/30, 57%), while the genes more highly expressed in DMCs were concentrated amongst the day 3 and day 4 DE genes (55/128, 43%).
evidence: This is based on comparison to prior studies on gene expression in nymphs versus DMCs.

claim: The timing and magnitude of gene expression changes during feeding may indicate whether gene expression will peak in the tick or continue rising once Bb is transmitted to the host.
source: These comparisons suggested that the timing and magnitude of gene expression changes during feeding may indicate whether gene expression will peak in the tick or continue rising once Bb is transmitted to the host.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the current study's results to prior studies.

claim: Amongst the cp32 genes that increased over feeding were members of the RevA, Erp, and Mlp families, which are known to increase expression during the bloodmeal.
source: Amongst the cp32 genes that increased over feeding were members of the RevA, Erp, and Mlp families, which are known to increase expression during the bloodmeal (Gilmore et al., 2001).
evidence: This is based on the RNA-seq data and supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Several phage genes were upregulated, including those encoding proteins annotated as phage terminases on cp32-3, cp32-4, and cp32-7 (BBS45, BBR45, and BBO44).
source: We also found several phage genes that were upregulated, including those encoding proteins annotated as phage terminases on cp32-3, cp32-4, and cp32-7 (BBS45, BBR45, and BBO44).
evidence: This is based on the RNA-seq data.

claim: In contrast to the upregulated genes, genes downregulated during feeding were more evenly distributed among the functional categories – including translation, protein degradation, transcription, and metabolism.
source: In contrast to the upregulated genes, genes downregulated during feeding were more evenly distributed among the functional categories – including translation, protein degradation, transcription, and metabolism – consistent with many of them being located on the chromosome.
evidence: This is based on functional categorization of differentially expressed genes shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Many of the outer surface protein genes that had increased expression over feeding were much less abundantly expressed than ospA, ospB, ospC, and bba59.
source: Many of the outer surface protein genes that we found had increased expression over feeding were much less abundantly expressed (Figure 4C and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of expression levels shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Even the genes that appeared to have low expression in population level measurements could play important roles in transmission if they are highly expressed in a small number of crucial cells.
source: However, even the genes that appeared to have low expression in these population level measurements could play important roles in transmission if they are highly expressed in a small number of crucial cells, such as those that ultimately escape the midgut.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential importance of lowly expressed genes in specific cell populations.

claim: The tick midgut environment is changing as the tick begins to digest its bloodmeal.
source: At the same time, the tick midgut environment is changing as the tick begins to digest its bloodmeal (Sonenshine and Anderson, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research on tick physiology.

claim: Tick proteins that interact with Bb would be present in the Bb-enriched samples.
source: Since our Bb enrichment process retained some tick material, we reasoned that tick proteins that interact with Bb would be present in these samples.
evidence: This is the reasoning behind using mass spectrometry on Bb-enriched samples.

claim: The distinct sets of tick proteins identified at each timepoint suggest dramatic changes occur in the Bb-infected tick midgut environment during feeding that may alter the landscape of tick-Bb interactions.
source: The distinct sets of tick proteins we identified at each timepoint suggest dramatic changes occur in the Bb-infected tick midgut environment during feeding that may alter the landscape of tick-Bb interactions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that different tick proteins were identified at different timepoints.

claim: 30 additional proteins identified one day after attachment were annotated with a cellular component as plasma membrane.
source: 30 additional proteins were annotated with a cellular component as plasma membrane.
evidence: This is based on functional annotation of proteins identified by mass spectrometry.

claim: These extracellular matrix and membrane proteins may be the most likely to directly interact with Bb during this timeframe and are candidates for tick proteins important in the Bb dissemination process.
source: These extracellular matrix and membrane proteins may be the most likely to directly interact with Bb during this timeframe and are candidates for tick proteins important in the Bb dissemination process.
evidence: This is speculation about which proteins are most likely to interact with Bb based on their localization.

claim: The proteins present in the changing tick environment may be key determinants of pathogen transmission as Bb remodels its outer surface while preparing to migrate through the tick to a new host.
source: The proteins present in the changing tick environment may be key determinants of pathogen transmission as Bb remodels its outer surface while preparing to migrate through the tick to a new host.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional importance of the identified tick proteins.

claim: Expression changes enable survival in the feeding tick.
source: For example, expression changes enable survival in the feeding tick (He et al., 2011), facilitate transmission across several internal compartments into the bloodmeal host (Kurokawa et al., 2020), and prime bacteria for successful infection of the next host (Kasumba et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Expression changes facilitate transmission across several internal compartments into the bloodmeal host.
source: For example, expression changes enable survival in the feeding tick (He et al., 2011), facilitate transmission across several internal compartments into the bloodmeal host (Kurokawa et al., 2020), and prime bacteria for successful infection of the next host (Kasumba et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Expression changes prime bacteria for successful infection of the next host.
source: For example, expression changes enable survival in the feeding tick (He et al., 2011), facilitate transmission across several internal compartments into the bloodmeal host (Kurokawa et al., 2020), and prime bacteria for successful infection of the next host (Kasumba et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The study focused analysis on 192 genes that changed twofold between one day after attachment and later days in feeding.
source: We focused our analysis on 192 genes that changed twofold between one day after attachment and later days in feeding.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach taken in the study.

claim: These genes were highly concordant with those found in previous studies probing transcriptional changes throughout the Bb enzootic cycle.
source: While these genes were highly concordant with those found in previous studies probing transcriptional changes throughout the Bb enzootic cycle (Caimano et al., 2019; Caimano et al., 2015; Drecktrah et al., 2015; Grassmann et al., 2023; Iyer et al., 2015; Ojaimi et al., 2003; Revel et al., 2002), our transcriptome profiles revealed changes in expression of 26 genes not observed in these previous studies.
evidence: This is based on comparison of the current study's results to multiple prior studies.

claim: The novel gene expression changes were concentrated in genes of unknown function and those encoding outer surface proteins.
source: These novel gene expression changes, like all of the 192 DE genes, were concentrated in genes of unknown function and those encoding outer surface proteins.
evidence: This is based on functional categorization of the differentially expressed genes.

claim: Efforts focused on uncovering the contribution of the genes of unknown function to the Bb life cycle could be groundbreaking for understanding the unique aspects of tick-borne transmission.
source: Although challenging to address, efforts focused on uncovering the contribution of the genes of unknown function to the Bb life cycle could be groundbreaking for understanding the unique aspects of tick-borne transmission.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential importance of studying genes of unknown function.

claim: These outer surface changes may play roles in the persistence of Bb in the tick, cell adhesion, or in immune evasion, either inside of the tick or later in the vertebrate host.
source: These outer surface changes may play roles in the persistence of Bb in the tick, cell adhesion, or in immune evasion, either inside of the tick or later in the vertebrate host (Kenedy et al., 2012).
evidence: This is speculation about the functional consequences of outer surface changes, supported by citation.

claim: It has long been observed that molecular interactions between pathogens and the midgut of their vectors are key determinants of transmission.
source: It has long been observed that molecular interactions between pathogens and the midgut of their vectors are key determinants of transmission (Barillas-Mury et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The hour-long enrichment procedure does not cause significant gene expression changes in cultured Bb.
source: While we confirmed that the hour-long enrichment procedure does not cause significant gene expression changes in cultured Bb, this may still influence gene expression in our ex vivo samples.
evidence: This is based on the control experiment comparing cultured Bb before and after enrichment.

claim: The enrichment procedure may still influence gene expression in ex vivo samples.
source: While we confirmed that the hour-long enrichment procedure does not cause significant gene expression changes in cultured Bb, this may still influence gene expression in our ex vivo samples.
evidence: This is speculation about potential limitations of the method.

claim: The transcriptional landscape of unfed ticks may be better probed through enrichment after RNA-seq library preparation such as TBDCapSeq or perhaps a combination of the two enrichment strategies.
source: The transcriptional landscape of unfed ticks may be better probed through enrichment after RNA-seq library preparation such as TBDCapSeq (Grassmann et al., 2023) or perhaps a combination of the two enrichment strategies.
evidence: This is speculation about alternative approaches to overcome the limitations of the current method.

claim: This type of antibody-based enrichment strategy is a simple and flexible technique that can probe gene expression from Bb from multiple timepoints in feeding ticks.
source: Despite these caveats, this type of antibody-based enrichment strategy is a simple and flexible technique that can probe gene expression from Bb from multiple timepoints in feeding ticks.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility and flexibility of the method developed in the study.

claim: With small modifications, this protocol may be able to assist in facilitating sequencing of Bb or other Borrelia species from other milieu or enrich other tick-borne bacterial species.
source: With small modifications, this protocol may be able to assist in facilitating sequencing of Bb or other Borrelia species from other milieu or enrich other tick-borne bacterial species.
evidence: This is speculation about potential applications of the method to other systems.

claim: The method has produced a transcriptomic resource providing critical insights into Bb population-level changes during the vector stage of its lifecycle.
source: Our method has produced a transcriptomic resource providing critical insights into Bb population-level changes during the vector stage of its lifecycle, which serves as a starting point for understanding the primary drivers of tick-borne transmission.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the contribution of the study.

claim: The work provides a foundational methodology that can be leveraged to greatly improve the resolution of tick–microbe studies.
source: Our work provides a foundational methodology that can be leveraged to greatly improve the resolution of tick–microbe studies, which may unearth surprising mechanistic insights into the unique lifestyles of tick-borne pathogens.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader impact and potential applications of the methodology.
